tasks.short: Monitor web intrusions and denial-of-service signals and report confirmed breaches.

steps.what: Inspect intrusion and denial-of-service alerts across web monitoring consoles
Correlate suspicious activity with request logs and confirm impact
Prepare the security breach report and supporting event references
Check and commit the final breach report and escalation priority
Send the approved breach report to the internal security responder

tasks.design: Configure a consolidated web-security view in the monitoring category of {OTHER}, grouping repeated alerts by service and time window. Reuse event references in a {HELPDESK} incident form, keep investigation and impact wording human, and send only the final report approved for the internal responder.
tasks.previous_blocker: Alerts and logs are scattered across web infrastructure and incident records.
tasks.enabler_now: Native grouping and incident connectors can remove console switching and repeated event metadata.
tasks.still_hard: Distinguishing attacks from traffic spikes and determining actual compromise.
tasks.human_edge: Judge uncertainty and escalate promptly without waiting for perfect attribution.

ambition.what: Review repeated low-severity web attack clusters at a daily operational triage.

tasks.altitude: Less console switching and report copying, with unchanged incident classification authority.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: deterministic alert grouping and incident forms can reduce repeated console work; compromise assessment remains analyst judgement.

assumptions: Boundary covers web monitoring, investigation and internal reporting; containment and statutory notifications are separate. No machine chooses a containment action.

Existing monitoring systems produce event ID, timestamp, service ID, rule ID, source address, request rate and severity. Deployment history is produced by the release process. Missing service mapping keeps alerts in the manual view.
s3 manually captures impact, uncertainty and recommended escalation from s2; native fields copy event metadata and references only. s4 checks the final text and recipient before authorizing dispatch.

Try native monitoring grouping and {HELPDESK} connectors first. Existing detection runtime earns no human saving; the estimate covers only assumed manual review navigation and repeated entry, to be measured.
Logging access, retention and employee consultation are assessed before rollout; no new staff performance scoring is added.
research_questions: Does grouping preserve distinct incidents and reduce navigation time without concealing evidence?

already_counted.description: Final breach report, priority and recipient review

incremental.description: Tune grouping keys and check failed incident notifications

approvals.approved_version: Final breach report fields reviewed immediately before committing the exact revision
Committed report revision, priority and responder destination checked in s4; changes require fresh approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central net 18.5%: 7.5 navigation, 8 report-entry and 5 dispatch hours removed, less 2 upkeep. Low assumes no navigation or report gain, leaving dispatch only. Investigation retains all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Identify and document web backup and recovery plans.

steps.what: Inspect application dependencies, backup configurations and recent restore evidence
Choose recovery order, checkpoints and escalation conditions for the web service
Write the backup and recovery runbook with configuration references
Walk through the final runbook against restore evidence and approve it
Publish the approved runbook to the restricted operational document collection

tasks.design: Use a versioned {DOCS} runbook template that reuses service and backup configuration references. The administrator chooses and writes recovery actions, checks the complete procedure against restore evidence, and approves its restricted publication; no model invents operational commands.
tasks.previous_blocker: Runbooks duplicate configuration details and become stale after service changes.
tasks.enabler_now: Native linked fields and versioned templates can reduce repeated documentation without automating recovery judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Dependencies and recovery objectives must be feasible under a real outage.
tasks.human_edge: Choose a safe recovery order and know when evidence is insufficient.
tasks.altitude: Less runbook formatting, unchanged disaster-recovery decision rights.

reach.learn: Emergency access and immutable backup controls

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: linked runbook templates can reuse configuration facts, but recovery actions need validated human procedures.

assumptions: Boundary is plan identification and documentation. New restore drills and backup configuration belong to task 14731; existing drill evidence is an input, not unpriced new testing.

Service owners already maintain service ID, dependencies and approved recovery objectives. Backup tooling supplies job ID, protected resources, retention and repository. s2 chooses order and checkpoints; s3 manually enters action instructions and fallback conditions.
No template invents commands from resource names. Missing procedure evidence requires manual development before approval. s3 retains 60% for this work; only linked facts and formatting shrink.
Test native {DOCS} templates first. Existing linked documentation earns no saving; assumed shares are unmeasured.
research_questions: Can the final runbook be followed without relying on undocumented administrator knowledge?

already_counted.description: Verify the final recovery sequence and evidence

incremental.description: Check linked facts after backup configuration changes

approvals.approved_version: Complete recovery runbook revision and configuration snapshot approved in s4; edits void publication authority

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High: twelve writing/formatting hours saved less two upkeep. Low: all runbook text is novel and no drafting benefit survives checks. Same-library publication, recovery design and walkthrough retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain backup configuration and application recovery readiness.

steps.what: Assess backup coverage and required application recovery changes
Prepare backup job or application configuration changes for disaster recovery
Review exact backup changes, exclusions and rollback before authorization
Apply the approved backup or recovery configuration change
Verify job completion and test recovery in an isolated environment
Check and record the recovery verification outcome

tasks.design: Configure approved backup policy profiles in the backup tooling category of {OTHER}, keeping target selection, exceptions and rollback explicit. The administrator approves the final configuration before application, tests recovery separately, and confirms the result in {HELPDESK}; scheduled backup runtime is not treated as saved labour.
tasks.previous_blocker: Per-service settings and exceptions require repeated configuration entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Native policy profiles can reuse known settings and apply a reviewed configuration revision.
tasks.still_hard: Application-consistent backups and successful restores across dependencies.
tasks.human_edge: Decide whether a successful job is actually sufficient recovery evidence.

ambition.what: Check recovery readiness after each material application configuration change.

tasks.altitude: Less configuration copying, unchanged recovery acceptance authority.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: backup policy profiles can reuse configuration settings; a successful scheduled job is not proof of recoverability.

assumptions: Boundary includes human backup coverage, configuration, change application, restore verification and its record. Existing scheduled backup execution and transfer duration are system runtime excluded from baseline shares.

Service owners supply protected resource IDs and approved recovery objectives. s2 manually captures job ID, targets, exclusions, retention, schedule, repository, application consistency option and rollback from s1 and the policy; profiles fill repeated settings only.

Missing or nonstandard application settings require manual preparation in s2. s3 checks operation meaning and exclusions, not just identifiers. s5 retains all restore test and human acceptance effort.
Try native policy profiles first. s6 saves only repeated job identifiers; outcome verification and final deliberate save remain counted. Estimates are provisional.
research_questions: Does a profile preserve application-specific exclusions and restore consistency on representative services?

incremental.description: Maintain approved profiles and test them after tooling updates

approvals.approved_version: Exact target list, configuration diff and rollback revision reviewed in s3; any edit invalidates application authority
Final recovery evidence and outcome fields checked immediately before saving their exact revision

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central net 19%: 10 preparation, 10 application and 1 repeated-record-entry hour removed, less 2 upkeep. Low assumes service-specific settings and existing automated application eliminate almost all new return; no runtime saving is claimed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Correct web defects found by tests or recommend their resolution.

steps.what: Reproduce the testing-identified problem and determine the intended behavior
Develop a corrective patch or concrete resolution recommendation in an isolated branch

loop.input: Reproduction, expected behavior, allowed source files and existing test conventions
loop.output: Bounded patch or recommendation diff in a disposable branch
loop.check: Administrator checks operation meaning, security, error handling and relevance; independent regression and reproduction tests run in s3
loop.stop: Two patch attempts maximum; no production credentials; unexplained changes or failed reproduction returns to manual correction
loop.why_not_simpler: Variable defects require source-code reasoning rather than a fixed replacement. Use native lint autofixes first for mechanical defects.

steps.what: Run reproduction, regression and security checks on the final candidate
Review the tested final diff and approve its integration or recommendation
Commit the approved correction or recommendation to the controlled internal repository

tasks.design: Use native lint fixes first, then a bounded draft patch in the source repository category of {OTHER} for defects requiring code reasoning. Keep reproduction and substantive tests with the administrator; integrate only the tested diff approved after final review, leaving production deployment to its existing release process.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every defect needs context-specific source reading and correction.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded coding assistance can propose a patch while existing test tooling checks behavior.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete tests and changes that appear to fix a symptom while breaking intended behavior.
tasks.human_edge: Define expected behavior and reject plausible but unsafe fixes.
tasks.altitude: Less initial patch writing, the same responsibility for correctness and release recommendations.

reach.task: Assess security effects of web fixes
reach.learn: Threat modeling and regression security tests

evidence.claim: The supplied digest describes GitHub Copilot completion and coding assistance with human oversight.

assumptions: Boundary is defect reproduction, correction and internal integration; production deployment is outside. No test runtime or release runtime is counted as human labour.
The tester supplies test ID, reproduction steps, observed result, expected behavior and build revision. s1 confirms these; absent reproduction or unclear intent stops model use.

s2 includes prompt preparation, source scoping, semantic review and editing. s3 retains all baseline test design, running supervision and result interpretation. A failed candidate returns to s2 and requires rerunning s3 before final approval.
First use native mechanical fixes; the loop is only for residual code reasoning. Shares and savings are provisional, with no claim that coding benchmarks predict this task.
research_questions: Does corrected patch-writing time fall after all review and retest effort is included?

already_counted.description: Scope the request and inspect and edit proposed corrections

incremental.description: Maintain allowed-file rules and evaluate coding-assistant changes

approvals.approved_version: Final correction diff hash, test evidence and integration target approved in s4; any edit or retest change invalidates approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: High:17.5 patch-writing hours saved less two upkeep; internal commit adds no saving. Low: correction overhead erases drafting gains and upkeep remains. Reproduction and tests retain full effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Use configured operations and bounded draft assistance while retaining security, recovery and correctness decisions.
role.ambitious_version: Review attack clusters and recovery readiness more often without delegating production authority to a model.
